note: Manifest v1, frozen. Hand-written rather than JSON Schema on purpose: the loader must refuse a duplicate JSON key and an unknown required field, and the contract's rule about `optional_metadata` is not expressible as a draft-07 constraint. python/tnca/manifest.py implements this file; it is not a second copy of it.

rules.optional_metadata: The ONLY place an ignorable extension may live. Nothing in it may affect an address, a resource, a completion or a numeric result, and the loader does not read it.
rules.serialisation: UTF-8, sort_keys, separators (',', ':'), no trailing newline, no NaN/Infinity. This is what `manifest_hash` is taken over, so two environments that build the same artifact produce the same bytes.

required.isa_version: the ISA the code is encoded for
required.source_kind: triton | tnca-ir -- which adapter produced it, never blurred
required.compiler_hash: hash of the compiler that emitted the code
required.source_hash: hash of the source it was emitted from
required.constexprs: the compile-time constants, which ARE part of the cache key
required.options: the compile options, which are too

required.config_hash: what the profile IS: elaboration parameters and capabilities
required.implementation_fingerprint: what the RTL IS. R2 changes the RTL, and a changed implementation may not wear R1's old hash
required.capabilities: the capabilities this code needs, each of which the device must report

required.segments: each with name, offset, length, sha256, alignment
required.entry_points: per role, or one shared dispatch entry stated as such
required.constant_segments: may be empty; same shape as code segments

required.signature: name, type, index, offset, size, alignment, direction, in frozen order
required.buffer_extents: for each pointer parameter, the minimum extent expression the runtime checks
required.alias_allowed: the pairs that may overlap. Anything not listed here may not

required.program_to_role: how a program's roles map onto the machine
required.dynamic_constraints: the bounds a launch is checked against, e.g. a loop trip count

required.shared_windows: the physical mapping of any window two roles share

required.completion_scope: what SUCCEEDED means for this kernel
required.error_contract: what a failure guarantees about the outputs
required.cross_program_dependency: false in v1; a kernel that needs another program to run first is refused at compile time

integrity.manifest_hash: sha256 over the canonical serialisation of every section except this field
integrity.segment_hashes: sha256 per segment, checked on load before a single instruction runs
integrity.claim: Integrity and compatibility. NOT authentication: this proves an artifact is the one that was built, not that whoever built it was entitled to.
